elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate for convenience (Agreement and/or Order Form)
elements.evidence: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience

elements.element: Notice period of 30 days, in writing
elements.evidence: upon 30 days' prior written notice to Vendor

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on such termination
elements.evidence: Vendor shall refund on a pro-rata basis any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term
upon 30 days' prior written notice (shorter than the 60–90 day fallback band)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: no early-termination fee appears in inserted 9.4 or elsewhere in Section 9

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate ... for convenience during a committed term" — no end-of-term Vendor right on 90 days' notice is granted

reasons: All four atomic preferred elements are present in the single inserted Section 9.4: Customer convenience right, 30 days' prior written notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term. Locked target level (preferred) is satisfied.

Fallback is not satisfied and need not be, as the drafter locked the preferred level; the 30-day notice sits below the 60–90 day band and no early-termination fee or end-of-term Vendor right is included (each of which would be a concession beyond the preferred bargain).

Minimality holds: a single concise insertion fills a genuinely absent clause, no untouched sentence was rewritten, no new exception or boilerplate was added, and numbering (9.4) fits cleanly between 9.3 and 9.5.
Intent is preserved: Sections 9.1–9.3 and 9.5 remain fully effective, only defined terms (Agreement, Order Form, Vendor, fees) are used, and no dangling mechanic is created.

Drafting note (not a defect for scoring): Section 2.1 states the take-or-pay commitment applies "without reduction or termination rights," so we would prefer to open 9.4 with "Notwithstanding Section 2.1," to remove any argument of tension; as drafted the specific, later termination right should control and the change is favourable to us.
